summary: Sarah H. Jacoby is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University and earned her PhD at the University of Virginia (1999–2007). She held posts at Columbia University (2006–2009) and Northwestern University (Associate Professor, 2009).

Sarah Harding (b. 1951) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche (1972) and Lama Tenpa. She held posts at Naropa University (~1992–2018; 2008) and served as a fellow at the Tsadra Foundation (~2000).

Sarah J. Horton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein and served as an Assistant Professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).
Sarah Merkle-Schneider is an Indology scholar. She studied at the University of Tübingen, where she earned an M.A. and held an M.A. post (attested 2026).

Sarah Shaw specializes in Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Lance S. Cousins. Her appointments include membership in Oxford's Faculty of Oriental Studies and Wolfson College, and honorary fellow at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2013).
Sarah Wells Brooks (1870–1941) was an Indologist. She studied at Radcliffe College in 1892 under Charles Rockwell Lanman.
Saraju Rath is an Indologist and linguist. She served as a teacher (attested 2010–2012) and held an attested post in 2022 at the International Institute for Asian Studies.

Sarasi Kumar Saraswati (1906–1983) was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He studied under Sivaprasad Bhattacharyya and Jitendra Nath Banerjea, and later held posts at The Asiatic Society (Librarian, 1943) and the University of Calcutta.

Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and Presidency College, Chennai, and under Ugyen Gyatso and Sengchen Lobzang Palden Chöpel. He was Director at Bhutia Boarding School (1874) and Bengal translator (1881–1904).
Sarat Sarma is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Manipur University under doctoral supervisor S. Shyamkishore Singh and teacher S. Lokendrajit Singh (attested 2006).

Sarath Piyananda Weerasekara specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He pursued a PhD in Sinhala Medium at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under doctoral supervisor Deshapriya Gunasena / G. A. Gamini (attested 2026).

Saroj Kanta Kar works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Utkal University (2007–2010, 2022), GITAM University (2010–2011), Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (2011), Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (2018–2021), and the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (2021–2022).

Saroja Bhate (b. 1942) is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She served as Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1989–2002) and as Honorary Secretary at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1999–2005).
Sarva Daman Singh works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and served as Professor of History at the University of Queensland (attested 1958, 1987).

Sarvepalli Gopal (1923–2002) was a historian. He studied at Mill Hill School, Madras Christian College, Presidency College, Chennai, University of Madras (~1940–1944), and Balliol College, Oxford (~1945–1951). He held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1971–1983).

Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Madras Christian College and Universities of Madras, Calcutta, and Delhi. He was Professor at Calcutta (1921–1931; 1937–1941) and Oxford (1936–1952), Vice-Chancellor at Andhra (1931–1936) and BHU (1939–1948), and Delhi Chancellor (1953–1962).

Sascha Ebeling is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held a post at the University of Cologne (attested 1999) and serves as Associate Professor and Director of Undergraduate Studies at the University of Chicago (attested 2026).

Saswati Mutsuddy is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned her MA, MPhil, and PhD at the University of Calcutta under Dipak Kumar Barua, and joined the university's Department of Pali in 2001.

Sati Shankar Dutta Pandey specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned his Master's and Ph.D. at Banaras Hindu University (1981–1990) and founded the Global Synergetic Foundation in 1992, serving as its Chief Functionary.
Satiranjan Sen is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University and was a Junior Research Fellow and Research Scholar at Visva-Bharati University.
